title: P2 execution conventions, allowlist protocol, commands and shared invariant models

sections.title: Rules every P2 item follows
sections.text:
P2 implements the recorded reference; it does not redesign it (owner M15, D16).

1. **Reference wins.** New and changed types, members, parameter names, defaults and generics are exactly those of `knowledge/contracts`; placement, owner, marker and action are exactly those of `knowledge/type-map`. A signature or placement that cannot be implemented as written is an amendment: stop the item, record a `plan.py log` friction entry with the evidence and ask the owner. Never ship a silent variant.
2. **No compatibility shims (D16).** No `class_alias`, no deprecated forwarding members, no adapters for old names, no special error text for removed keys. A removed supported symbol is simply gone and gets one line in the migration instruction.
3. **Interim placement (D17).** A module-owned type that P2 creates or renames gets its type-map target FQCN and lives where PSR-4 `AzGuard\ → packages/core/src` puts it (`src/Scopes/Internal/ScopeEvaluator.php`, `src/Audit/AuditOptions.php`). Files are not moved into `packages/core/modules/` (P3). Types whose row says `move / P3` or `close+move / P3` keep their current FQCN in P2.
4. **Publication.** Every type an item creates or whose FQCN it changes carries the attribute of its type-map marker (`#[Api(since: …)]`, `#[Spi(kind: SpiKind::Implement|Call, since: …)]`) or none for `internal`; `since: '1.0'` for new or reshaped types, `'0.7'` only for an existing type whose supported shape the item leaves unchanged (knowledge/contracts#rules). Constructors documented as built by core and the members `knowledge/contracts` lists as internal carry `@internal`. Every attributed enum carries exactly one `@closed`/`@open` tag (D15). After any change of a supported type run `composer api:manifest` and commit both manifests.
5. **Core calls `Spi(Implement)` methods positionally (I20).** Parameter names of `Api` callables are covered: keep the names written in `knowledge/contracts`.
6. **Allowlists are report mode** (`#allowlists`): fix → remove the entry in the same commit; a new entry only with owner P3 and only when the type map assigns the fix to P3.
7. **Snapshots are regression guards, not promises (D16).** When an item changes a pinned format on purpose (manifest, commands.json, config defaults, doctor checks, events, resources), regenerate that fixture in writer mode in the same commit and list every changed fixture in the item result notes. An unexplained fixture change is a defect.
8. **Migration instruction.** Each item appends its lines to `docs/upgrade.md`, section `## From 0.7 to 1.0 (instructions for AI agents)` (created by P2.1): one bullet per removed/renamed supported symbol, member, DSL call, config key, command behavior or identity value, in the form `Find: <pattern> → Replace: <new form>` with a grep-able pattern; at most one sentence of explanation. Internal moves are not listed.
9. **Tests.** Existing tests are updated mechanically for renamed API; assertions are never weakened, deleted or skipped to get green. A test that observed retired behavior (for example `boot()` being called) is rewritten to assert the new rule. Every new rule gets a negative test that fails without the rule.
10. **Ownership oracle** `tests/Arch/Fixtures/target-map.json` is not edited (D14). If a P2 change truly needs a different row, that is an amendment (rule 1).
11. **No new mechanism** beyond the reference: no macros, `__call`, service locator, module bus, plugin-id checks, `class_exists` switches or priority sorting (knowledge/architecture#extension-system).

sections.title: Report-mode allowlists and owner phases
sections.text:
P1 installed report-mode checks: current violations must equal the allowlist exactly — a new violation fails, a fixed violation still listed fails as stale.

| File | Invariant | P2 duty |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `tests/Arch/Allowlists/i2.json` | I2 core → module references | remove every entry an item fixes, whatever its owner phase; the 2 entries with owner P2 (`Panel.php`, `PanelBuilder.php` importing `AssignmentScopePolicy`) disappear in P2.7 |
| `tests/Arch/Allowlists/i3.json` | I3 module ↔ module / Filament | stays empty |
| `tests/Arch/Allowlists/i4.json` (created by P2.1) | I4 modules, Filament, stubs use only attributed symbols/members | entries with owner P2 disappear by P2.14; owner P3 only where the type map moves the fix to P3 (audit prune, scaffold config) |
| `tests/Arch/Allowlists/i5.json` | I5 one autoload owner, no `src/Scopes`, `src/Audit`, `src/DevTools`, `src/Plugins/Audit` | `packages/core/src/Audit` is added with owner P3 when the first `AzGuard\Audit\` type appears (D17) |
| `tests/Fixtures/Parity/i7-allowlist.json` | I7 no scope declaration | stays empty |
| `tests/Fixtures/Parity/i9-findings-0.7.0.json` | I9 directory vs write | F1 and F2 (owner P2) are fixed in P2.9; the file then holds no finding and the parity test asserts zero disagreements |
| `tests/Fixtures/InactiveCost/allowlist.json` | I13 inactive cost | `ChangeJournal` module-service entry disappears in P2.11; `audit_log` table entry stays (P3) |

Owner phase of a new entry: `Ownership::removingPhase()` of the referencing and referenced rows. An entry whose removing phase is P2 must be fixed by the item, not listed. At the P2 exit (P2.14) every list holds only owner-P3 entries.

sections.title: Validation commands and environment
sections.text:
Run from the repository root. Database services (brief environment): `PGSQL_PORT=55432 MYSQL_PORT=53306 docker compose up -d postgres mysql mariadb`; export `PGSQL_PORT=55432 MYSQL_PORT=53306` before every pgsql/mysql/mariadb command, otherwise tests hit host services. Use the `default` Docker context.

| Purpose | Command |
|:--|:--|
| Architecture checks | `php -d memory_limit=1G vendor/bin/pest tests/Arch --fail-on-skipped` |
| Parity, I7, inactive cost, P1 snapshots | `php -d memory_limit=1G vendor/bin/pest tests/Feature/Parity tests/Feature/InactiveCost tests/Regression/Baseline070 --fail-on-skipped` |
| Full SQLite suite | `composer test` |
| Drivers | `PGSQL_PORT=55432 composer test:pgsql`, `MYSQL_PORT=53306 composer test:mysql`, `composer test:mariadb` |
| Engine race/consistency suites | `PGSQL_PORT=55432 composer test:engines:pgsql`, `MYSQL_PORT=53306 composer test:engines:mysql`, `composer test:engines:mariadb` |
| Static analysis, style, refactor | `composer analyse`, `composer lint:check`, `composer refactor:check` |
| Manifests | `composer api:check` (fresh) |
| Type coverage | `composer test:types` |

From P2.1 on `composer analyse` exits 0 (P2.1 fixes the two pre-existing errors in `RoutesChecks.php:106` and `AuthorizesActions.php:91`). Diagnostics such as single-test reruns are not acceptance evidence.

sections.title: Assignment-scope check order and failure mapping (shared by P2.7–P2.10)
sections.text:
One interpretation for scalar, batch, SQL, directory and write (knowledge/architecture#scope-boundary, knowledge/contracts#scopes). Core owns steps 1–5; the evaluator is called only at step 6 and can only narrow.

| Step | Owner | Scalar / batch decision | Write admission (`ChangeValidator`) | Directory (Assignment/Inspection) | Visibility |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 tenant mode | core | `TenantMode` | same | same | same |
| 2 scope mode | core `AssignmentScopeMode` from `Panel::scopeDeclaration()` (null = `None`) | `None` + non-global → deny `assignment_scope_not_accepted`; `Required` + global → deny `assignment_scope_required` | `AssignmentScopeNotAcceptedException` / `AssignmentScopeRequiredException` | no non-global option under `None` (fixes I9 F1) | unsupported never broadens |
| 3 declared alias | core | undeclared → deny | reject | alias without directory → empty directory | — |
| 4 `AssignmentScopeDefinition::resolve()` | core calls definition | refusal → deny/failure; null → not accepted | reject | option omitted | — |
| 5 structural verification | core | ref, owner tenant, record model and canonical key equal the request | same; plus target tenant membership (fixes I9 F2) | same as write | core joins resource branch, tenant guard |
| 6 eligibility | evaluator `allows()` / `allowsMany()` / `eligibleContexts()` | false → deny; exception → deny `assignment_scope_filter_error` (failure distinguishable) | false → `AssignmentScopeNotAcceptedException` with cause | same `allows(Assignment)` as write | `false` → `VisibilityNotSupportedException` reason `scope_query` |

Envelope (core only): selected scope + tenant-wide scope when context non-global and mode ≠ `Isolated` + global-tenant variants for declared global roles. `allowsMany()` answer count ≠ check count fails the whole set. Revocation, expiry, touch and role-key migration never consult steps 4–6 (I7). No evaluator in the declaration → eligibility is structural only and visibility over scoped resources is unsupported.

sections.title: Transactional participant invariant model (P2.11)
sections.text:
**Invariant.** For every root commit of a write operation, the authority rows, revisions/epoch and every participant row of that operation become durable together, each participant row carries the `eventId` of exactly one event that is dispatched after that root commit, and nothing of a discarded attempt (exception, rollback, nested host rollback, deadlock retry) remains or is published.

**Enforcement points.**
- `ChangePipeline::operate()` builds one `AccessEvent` per effect once (`ChangeEventPublisher::events()` is called exactly once per change result) and keeps the list; the same objects go to `ChangeRecord`s and to the after-commit dispatch.
- After the last change of the operation, if at least one effect exists, each participant of the panel is called in declaration order inside the same `writer->transaction()` with `non-empty-list<ChangeRecord>` in effect order and an `Changes\Internal\OperationRows` bound to the active `StorageMutation`.
- `OperationRows::insert()` accepts only a base table name declared by that participant's `tables()`, only scalar/null column values, only while its call window is open; otherwise `UnsupportedDirectWriteException`. It writes through the mutation (operation connection + storage prefix), never returning a builder or connection.
- Compilation rejects (`DefinitionException`): participants on a panel without the core writer; `tables()` naming a core table (`permissions`, `role_grants`, `permission_grants`, `panel_state`, `subject_revisions`, `storage_state`); two participants of one panel declaring the same table; a non-`ChangeParticipant` handler.

**Bypass routes closed.** The public `ChangeJournal` sink and `DatabaseSource::appendJournal()` are removed; a change pipe has no writer handle; `meta` is not a mailbox; participants never receive `StorageMutation`.

**Interfering operation pairs (must stay correct).**
| Pair | Expected |
|:--|:--|
| participant exception ↔ authority writes | whole operation rolls back; no event, no cache publication |
| deadlock retry ↔ participant rows | rows of the discarded attempt rolled back; participants run again with the new attempt's events |
| host transaction on the same connection ↔ nested operation | rows join the host transaction; events wait for the host root commit; host rollback discards all |
| no-op repeat ↔ participants | no call, no row, no event |
| `azguard:audit:prune` (still `ChangePipeline::pruneJournal` under the panel lock until P3) ↔ concurrent grant | unchanged 0.7.0 lock order; P3 changes prune |
| storage on a dedicated connection ↔ host transaction | host transaction does not cover AzGuard writes (documented) |

**Checks.** I6 capability tests, I11 suites re-targeted to the participant (`tests/Feature/Plugins/Audit`, `TransactionPropertiesTest`, `NestedMutationTest`, `ChangeRaceTest`), I12 after-commit tests, engine race suites on pgsql/mysql/mariadb.
